title: Concept of Social Capital
text:
Social capital refers to the networks of relationships and mutual trust that exist within a community or group. It represents the collective resources embedded in social structures, such as shared norms, information flow, and reciprocal obligations between individuals.

High levels of social capital are often correlated with improved civic engagement, economic growth, and better public health outcomes within a population. For example, strong neighborhood ties can facilitate access to local job opportunities or emergency aid, acting as a buffer against systemic shocks.

Academically, the concept moves beyond merely counting connections; it emphasizes the quality of those relationships—the depth of trust and reciprocity—as crucial components for societal functioning.
